question: Can the sharp blade-root corner be replaced by a constant-radius blend and a converged peak stress measured?
answer: The blend builds and verifies, but no constant-radius blend of the blade root is solvable: its run-out at the blade leading and trailing edges self-intersects at 2.0 mm and produces inverted quadratic elements at 1.0 mm. A converged blended peak is not established.

geometry.accepted_on: blend surface: face count, blend area, sampled curvature radius, blade-to-blade symmetry
geometry.never_accepted_on: solid volume - the eleven sequential blade unions drift by order 10-20 mm3 in a 229,000 mm3 solid while the blend adds only 30-120 mm3 per blade, so a volume difference cannot resolve it

radii_mm.mesher_error: PLC Error: a segment and a facet intersect - the blend surfaces self-intersect

solver_refusal.cause: C3D10 mid-side nodes fold where the blend runs out at the blade leading and trailing edges, the region whose sampled curvature radius is about 0.03 mm against the 1 mm nominal

occ_healing_rejected.reason: Geometry.OCCSewFaces discards the volume and leaves an empty 3D mesh behind a generate(3) that raises nothing, on the sharp rotor as much as the blended one

blended_ladder_cost.note: the blend element size follows curvature sampling N as about 2*pi*r/N, so a ladder on a 1 mm blend must drive N

reference_point.memory: more than 9 GB; failed closed in a 9 GB container

blended_ladder_cost.verdict: the coarsest useful rung is 2.4x the reference point and a ladder needs three; not runnable on this host

next_steps: Treat the blend run-out: taper the radius to zero at the blade leading and trailing edges instead of carrying a constant radius into the corner.
Then submodel: solve the full rotor coarse and re-solve one blade sector with those boundary displacements, which makes a resolved blend affordable without a larger host.
limitations: No root stress and no root margin are established for this part.
The sharp-root peak is a singularity; see blade-root-convergence.json.
Boundary conditions remain assumptions: the joint to the bearing hub is not measured.
